llm.summary: The skill's code and SKILL.md are coherent with a Notion-based long-term-memory tool, but the registry metadata omits the Notion credential and local config requirements and the package includes executable scripts that will read/write local config and Notion — review before installing or granting tokens.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Notion LTM, emotion/state, journal, subagent payload generation) match what the code and SKILL.md do: creating/searching/writing Notion databases and maintaining a local ~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json. However the registry metadata claims no required env vars or config paths while SKILL.md and all scripts clearly require a Notion token and a local config file — that mismatch is unexpected and reduces trust.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are narrowly focused on Notion operations and local config management (create DBs, write events/emotions/state/journal, query data_sources, produce subagent JSON). The scripts read NOTION_API_KEY (or fallback file ~/.config/notion/api_key), write ~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json, and append logs under the skill's state folder. They do not call unrelated external services beyond Notion nor attempt to modify other skills or system-wide settings. One element to note: the skill generates sessions_spawn payloads for subagent spawning (it does not itself call a gateway spawn endpoint), so review how you might use that output.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no remote install/download step in the package (no install spec); the repository is script-based and runs local JS/Python files. No external archives or URL downloads are executed by install — lower delivery risk. Nevertheless these scripts will run locally and make network requests to Notion when invoked.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md and all code expect a Notion API token (NOTION_API_KEY / NOTION_TOKEN / NOTION_API_TOKEN) and a local config at ~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json; the registry metadata incorrectly lists no required env vars or config paths. Requiring a Notion token is proportionate for a Notion integration, but the metadata omission is an inconsistency users should not ignore.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Flags: always is false, model invocation is allowed (default). The skill writes only to its own config (~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/) and uses the Notion token to create/read DBs; it does not request persistent elevated platform privileges or alter other skills. Autonomous invocation combined with credential access increases blast radius, but that is expected for useful integrations and not set to always:true.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package implements a Notion-based long-term memory + emotion/state system and contains runnable scripts that will create databases and write/read data in your Notion workspace. Before installing: 1) Be aware the code requires a Notion integration token (NOTION_API_KEY) and writes a local config at ~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json — the registry entry omitted these, which is suspicious. 2) Only grant a Notion token scoped to the specific parent page/databases (create an integration with limited access to the page), not a full-account token. 3) Inspect the scripts yourself (they are included) or run them in a sandboxed environment to confirm behavior. 4) If you accept it, keep tokens in environment variables (or the dedicated ~/.config/notion/api_key file) and rotate/remove the token if you uninstall. 5) The skill can produce subagent sessions_spawn payloads but does not itself call a gateway; ensure you control how those payloads are used. If you do not trust the unknown source or cannot limit the Notion token scope, do not install or run these scripts.
